group_assessment.weighting: A multi-centre clinical-genetics consortium reporting a retrospective diagnostic-laboratory series, and the senior author's single WWOX publication. There is no experimental arm of any kind: every statement in the paper is a clinical observation or a variant call. That is the right provenance for a phenotype and endpoint question and the wrong provenance for a mechanism, which is how the reading uses it - no mechanistic proposition is taken from it.

queue.target: Piard et al. 2019 - the comparator cohort this paper measures itself against on four endpoints (age at seizure onset, respiratory involvement, growth retardation and microcephaly rates, eye contact)
queue.question: Does the comparator cohort quantify any of these endpoints with an instrument, or are its rates counts of qualitative descriptors too? The disagreements this paper reports - 80 percent against 40 percent respiratory, its own near-universal failure to thrive against 6 percent growth retardation - are interpretable only if both cohorts ascertained the endpoint the same way.
queue.status: open - that cohort is held and read in this repository, so the question is asked of the existing reading, not of a new acquisition

queue.target: Havali et al. 2021 - head circumference below -3 SD in all six patients of another cohort
queue.question: Is that a measured series of occipitofrontal circumferences with ages, i.e. a usable growth-endpoint denominator for WOREE, or a count of a clinical label? Cited here and read nowhere in this repository.

queue.target: Johannsen 2018, Ko 2018, Riva 2022 - the three prior ketogenic-diet reports this paper cites as 'varying degrees of success'
queue.question: What endpoint did each use, over what window, with what exposure denominator? Three citations carrying the word success are the whole published base of the only dietary early-benefit observation in WOREE, and none of the three is read for its diet arm here.

verbatim_locators.abstract_anchoring_waived: The abstract of this paper is three sentences of phenotype summary and carries none of the propositions below. It names the ketogenic diet once, as 'epilepsy that responded to a ketogenic diet in three patients', and that sentence is the overstatement this reading exists to bound: it carries no endpoint, no exposure denominator, no window, no comparator and no developmental outcome, and the abstract contains no EEG, growth, visual, sleep or mortality value at all. Anchoring these entries to it would attach each measured bound to the sentence it narrows.

entries.proposition: On the delivered surface the ketogenic-diet benefit is a clinician-reported improvement in seizure control in three named patients: the Discussion sentence carries no count, score or instrument, and neither does Table 1, whose Epilepsy row records only seizure types and the fact of a response. Whether a seizure quantity is reported in the per-patient narratives is NOT COVERED - chunks 3-17 are absent from this surface.
entries.snippet: However, the institution of a ketogenic diet in patients 1, 2, and 4 notably improved seizure control.

contradicts_locator.what_changed: OVERSHOOT repaired: the absence clause said the paper has no counted, scored or instrumented endpoint; the per-patient narratives (chunks 3-17) are not on this surface, so the absence is now asserted OF THE DELIVERED SURFACE and the narratives are declared NOT COVERED.

entries.proposition: The authors hedge AND recommend, and both halves are the source's: they decline to assert the effect and name cohort size as the reason, then state in the same chunk that the findings 'may help to improve the control of epilepsy in certain patients', report the three responders in the abstract, and conclude that the diet 'should be considered for the treatment of epilepsy in these patients'. Carrying only the hedge makes the paper more cautious than it is.
entries.snippet: It may be premature to assert the potential beneficial effects of a ketogenic diet as they need to be evaluated carefully in a larger cohort. However, these findings suggest that the implementation of a ketogenic diet may help to improve the control of epilepsy in certain patients with WOREE syndrome.

entries.proposition: Two of the three diet responders are previously published individuals NAMED BY THE SOURCE, so a pooled count across WOREE series double-counts them. The paper declares three new and two previously published patients; Table 1's last row attributes patients 2 and 4 to Piard et al. (2019) - and chunk 18 attributes patient 4's homozygous exon-6 deletion to Dharmadhikari et al. (2019) - while patients 1, 2 and 4 are the three described as responding to the diet. Any pooled count must therefore name which individuals it is counting.

contradicts_locator.what_changed: UNDERSHOOT repaired, and the correction REVERSES the direction of the caution. The entry said the surface does not say which two patients were previously published; it does, in Table 1's last row and in chunk 18, and the two it names are BOTH diet responders. The boundary is therefore not 'we cannot tell, so do not pool' but the stronger and more specific 'two of the three responders are named prior individuals, so any pooled count double-counts them and must name which'. Note the attribution row's own header scope: it reports whether a VARIANT was reported elsewhere, so the row names the candidates and the three-new/two-published split comes from the text.
